title: The sunnah prayers
hookLine: regular extra units before and after the obligatory ones

cards: Better than the world and everything in it. That's a big claim to make about two short units of prayer, said quietly in a dark bedroom before the dawn prayer, with the alarm still blinking and nobody watching.

Aishah reports the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, saying exactly that about the two units before the dawn prayer, in Sahih Muslim, number 725. Not the obligatory prayer. The small extra one before it.
Today, the prayers that sit around the obligatory ones like a frame around a picture.

teach.b: The word is rawatib, the regular ones: the voluntary prayers the Prophet ﷺ kept attached to the obligatory prayers, some just before, some just after. Not required, but not random either.

teach.h: UMM HABIBAH: TWELVE, A HOUSE IN THE GARDEN.
teach.b: In Sahih Muslim, number 728, his wife Umm Habibah reports him saying that whoever prays twelve units a day and night, beyond the obligatory, will have a house built for them in the garden.
And Umm Habibah adds that she never stopped praying them after she heard it.

teach.h: THE TWO BEFORE DAWN, KEPT MOST CAREFULLY.
teach.b: Jami at-Tirmidhi, number 415, lays out where those units fall: four before the noon prayer and two after it, two after the sunset prayer, two after the night prayer, and two before dawn.
Another companion, Ibn Umar, in Sahih al-Bukhari, number 1180, remembers ten, with two before noon instead of four.
The schools follow these reports in slightly different ways, and Shia practice keeps its own pattern of daily voluntary prayers. Among all of them, one pair gets special weight.
Aishah says, in Sahih al-Bukhari, number 1169, that the Prophet ﷺ was not more careful about any voluntary prayer than the two before dawn. Why pray what isn't required?

teach.h: BETTER THAN THE WORLD AND ALL IN IT.
teach.b: One answer is in the word sunnah itself: following how he actually prayed, not only what was demanded.

Another is in a hadith in Sunan Abu Dawud, number 864: on the day of reckoning, if the obligatory prayers fall short, the voluntary ones are looked to, to make up what's missing. The frame protects the picture.

how: Muslims who keep the rawatib pray short voluntary units before or after the obligatory prayers, at home or in the mosque, following the pattern their school teaches, and give particular care to the two units before the dawn prayer.

o: the regular voluntary prayers kept around the obligatory ones
the five obligatory prayers said at fixed times each day
long night prayers said only in the month of Ramadan

games.q: the sunnah prayers — tap the pairs.
p: twelve units, a house in the garden

s: they're voluntary, the regular extra units the Prophet kept around the obligatory ones.
the companions' reports all give the same number
Umm Habibah's hadith speaks of twelve; Ibn Umar remembered ten.
the two units before dawn get special weight
Aishah: he was not more careful about any voluntary prayer than those two.

games.q: you're Umm Habibah, and you've just heard that twelve voluntary units a day bring a house in the garden. what do you do?
o: leave it, since they aren't required.
games.why: in Muslim 728 she says she never stopped praying them after she heard it.

practice: Picture tomorrow morning: the alarm, the dark, the minute before the dawn prayer or before your day begins, and see yourself adding something small and extra there, before the main thing.

If you pray, those are the two units before fajr, and you can settle now on praying them; if you don't, choose a two-minute habit to set before the first big task of your day. Then sit quietly with the decision made.

wordCard.voice: Rawatib. The regular voluntary prayers, before and after the obligatory ones, with the two before dawn kept most carefully of all. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the regular ones, the sunnah prayers tied to the obligatory.

carryVoice: Your line: the sunnah around it. Small, extra, and kept, the way Umm Habibah kept hers. Up next: the odd prayer.
